name: PROSPERITY
materialIdentity: A bare hillside claim: mud, rock and something unidentified, a leaning stake, a dark old hole; night, the town's hour (errata 98)
note: Rooms 23 and 24, doc 20: Thad's claim and its hole (one room, CLAUDE.md), above the road to the claims. Reached by the road's way up and by the map, only while Thad holds the Company's map (doc 57 A4). THE HOLE's LISTEN is one of the three lines that must never be marked (invariant 3, doc 05): it is compiled like every other line. A5, the raccoon, plays here (doc 54); F1 in Act IV. LOOK_AT.say: Not until the air clears. Possibly not until the season does.

repeat: He has arranged the hole to his satisfaction. There is a pine cone positioned with real intent.
We have looked at each other for some time. He is winning, in the sense that he is comfortable.
then: He was in my hole before it was my hole, which he clearly regards as decisive.

LISTEN_TO.say: Not until the air clears. Possibly not until the season does.
Breathing. Slowly. In a way I would describe as editorial.
repeat: A small, contented grinding. He is eating something, and it was mine.
He's breathing at me again. I've been reviewed and found tenantable.

USE.say: Not until the air clears. Possibly not until the season does.
Not while he's in the hole. I have seen how that goes, and so has Mr. Pratt's thumb.

USE.say: Thad takes off his coat and drops it over him. There is a great deal of coat, and then a great deal of raccoon.
then: I have him. I am not sure which of us is winning.

PICK_UP.say: With my hands? Mr. Pratt tried that, and now he has respect.

TALK_TO.say: Not until the air clears. Possibly not until the season does.
He has heard me. He has decided against it.
repeat: I asked after his health. He ate something I hadn't known was edible.
We have reached an understanding. He understands it and I do not.

overrides.PICK_UP: No. He is in residence, and I am not his landlord in any sense he recognizes.
overrides.PUSH: I'm not going to push a raccoon further into a hole he already likes. That's encouragement.
overrides.USE: He is not a tool. He is barely a tenant.

LOOK_AT.say: Somewhere past that stake is the most famous piece of ground in the territory.
repeat: A boundary stake, older than mine and sunk deeper. Someone meant it.
On that side, the most valuable ground in the territory. On this side, mine. The raccoon cannot tell the difference, and has not tried.
then: It looks exactly like this piece of ground.

repeat: Wind, crossing from his land to mine without a survey.
Exactly the same. I have listened for the difference twice now, and the difference is the price.

LOOK_AT.say: Prosperity. Named by a liar, bought by a fool, and correct the entire time. There is a sermon in that and Sowerby cannot have it.
A stake with a number on it, and the number is mine! My first property, my first anything. Beyond it, forty feet of land that is legally, indisputably mine.
repeat: The number is painted on with confidence and very little paint.
It leans. I've straightened it twice, and it's gone back to leaning, which I respect as a position.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wind. It is not impressed either.
repeat: The stake creaks in the wind like a man trying to remember something.
Wind again. It comes through here on its way to somewhere better.

USE.say: I stood beside my stake, firmly. He stood beside his. Mine has the number. His has him.
USE.sceneLine: docs/113-act-two-scenes.md::### B · The stake · **THE CLAIM MARKER** · *while Pratt is on the claim - USE

PICK_UP.say: Carry it off and I have jumped my own claim. He would thank me, briefly.
PICK_UP.sceneLine: docs/113-act-two-scenes.md::### B · The stake · **THE CLAIM MARKER** · *while Pratt is on the claim - PICK UP

PULL.say: If I pull it up myself he has only to stand here. He is very good at standing here.
PULL.sceneLine: docs/113-act-two-scenes.md::### B · The stake · **THE CLAIM MARKER** · *while Pratt is on the claim - PULL

then.speaker: pratt_jump
then.line: Pratt drives his own, one stroke.

PUSH.sceneLine: docs/113-act-two-scenes.md::### B · The stake · **THE CLAIM MARKER** · *while Pratt is on the claim - PUSH

overrides.PUSH: Mine now, lean and all. I have decided the lean is jaunty.
overrides.TALK_TO: 'Prosperity,' I told it, 'you and I are going to be the punchline of something.' I was righter than I knew.

LOOK_AT.say: A creek, low and brown, running past the foot of my claim and declining to stop.
repeat: Men upstream pan it every day. By the time it reaches me it has been thoroughly searched.
It is the only thing on my property that is going anywhere.

LISTEN_TO.say: Water over stones, talking to itself the way water does, cheerfully and without content.
repeat: The same water. It has said nothing new since I arrived, which makes it the most reliable voice in the district.
A pan scraping, far upstream. Somebody hoping. The creek carries that down too.

LOOK_AT.say: Not until the air clears. Possibly not until the season does.
The hole is warm. It has been warm since the day I bought it: warm air, out of solid rock, all autumn.
then: Air does not come out of rock. It comes through it.
LOOK_AT.sceneLine: docs/57-puzzle-completion.md::## F1 · One last look at Prosperity · Act IV

LOOK_AT.say: The hole. The warm air. I evicted a raccoon from the front door of a fortune and apologized to neither of us.
A hole. Forty feet of my property goes down into it and does not come back.
repeat: The edges are old and smooth. Whatever dug this was in no hurry.
Forty feet of my land, and this is the only part of it that has shown any initiative.

LISTEN_TO.say: Not until the air clears. Possibly not until the season does.
Air. Moving. Warmer than the day. The same words as always; I am only now hearing what they were saying.
Air. Moving. It's warmer than the day.
repeat: Air. Moving. It's warmer than the day.
Air. Moving. It's warmer than the day.

USE.say: Not until the air clears. Possibly not until the season does.
My coat over the hole would only make it warmer. He would write to thank me.

overrides.CLOSE: I can't close a hole. I can only fill it, and I don't have anything to spare, including — on some mornings — the inclination.
overrides.TALK_TO: I said good morning down it. The echo said it back warmer than the town does.

LOOK_AT.say: The ridge above the claims, bare to the sky.
repeat: There is a path up it, worn by men going to look at what they cannot have.
It was here before the town and expects to be here after. It has the patience of a creditor.
then: From up there, I am told, you can see the whole district and none of its prospects.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wind along the top, steady as a held note.
repeat: The wind again, a little sharp. Somebody should see to that.
Nothing coming down from it. Whatever is up there is keeping it to itself.

LOOK_AT.say: Approximately forty percent mud, thirty percent rock, and thirty percent a substance I haven't yet identified.
repeat: Having stood in it, I can report on the unidentified thirty percent. It is cold, and it is personal.
This is the mud I own. I keep expecting to feel differently about it than about other mud. I do, a little. It's mine.
It sucks at my boot as I lift it. Possessive, for something I bought.
A slow settling. It has nowhere else to be, and neither, it turns out, do I.

overrides.USE: I did use it. I filed it. It is the most administrated mud in the territory.

exits.name: THE ROAD

LOOK_AT.say: The way back down to the road, past my claim post. Forty feet is not far, and I have walked it a great many times.
repeat: The path down is worn mostly by me, and a little by a raccoon.
Down there are the town, the queue, and everybody who knows exactly what this claim is worth. They're wrong. I can feel it.

LISTEN_TO.say: The road below, empty, and the wind deciding which way to go along it.
repeat: Dry scrub rattling. It's the busiest thing on the hill.
Far down, a cart on the road, going somewhere with something in it.

exits.note: Doc 20: the way back down to the road. NO DOCUMENT WRITES IT a LOOK or LISTEN: a stub exit (doc 36 Q166). Leaving ends the raccoons' meeting and the fumes (doc 54 A5: 'gone the next time Thad enters'; 'until he leaves and returns').

exits.name: PRATT'S CLAIM

LOOK_AT.say: Next door, Pratt's claim, swept and squared. Even his trickle of water runs in a straight line.
repeat: The trickle that crosses from his side is the only thing on his claim that has ever come toward mine of its own accord.
There's a fire over there most nights. He works by it, or sits by it and watches my side.

LISTEN_TO.say: Water running over stones next door, in a hurry to be somewhere else.
repeat: His fire, popping. It's the only warm sound on this side of the hill.
Nothing from Pratt. Pratt is quiet the way a man is quiet when he's listening.

exits.note: Doc 20: Pratt's claim, next door (doc 04 PRA_A1: 'beside Prosperity'), past the creek at the right. NO DOCUMENT WRITES IT a LOOK or LISTEN: a stub exit (errata 97 C). Leaving ends the meeting and the fumes, as the road does.

exits.name: THE TUNNEL

LOOK_AT.say: My tunnel. I dug it. It goes down further than anything I've done in my life, in every sense.
repeat: Warm air coming up out of it, which is not what holes in the ground are supposed to do.
The raccoon's hole, enlarged by a man with a pickaxe and nothing left to lose.

LISTEN_TO.say: Warm air breathing out of it, slow and steady.
repeat: Loose earth trickling down the sides and settling in the dark.
Nothing coming up but the warm air. It doesn't say where it has been.

exits.note: Doc 57 F1: 'Room 34 opens below the hole.' Once the three days' digging is done (T_DUG_DOWN), the hole's mouth is the way down: a small exit inside THE HOLE, whose own lines stay its own (invariant 3: its LISTEN is never marked). Room 34 writes THE TUNNEL; from up here it is a stub (errata 72 F, 99 H).

entrances.note: Up from the road, at left.
Up from the road, at left.
From the map, as from the road.
Back from next door, at right (errata 97 C).
Up the rope and out of the hole (errata 99 H).

TALK_TO.say: Madame Ozymandia. You're a long way from your tent.
repeat: No fee today, Madame?
I'll leave you to it, then.

figureLight.note: Errata 238, as errata 207 B graded four figures into their night: Prosperity is night, and act3-estate-sale's hen was painted in daylight browns and its raccoon halfway out in neutral greys, a little lighter than the sitting raccoon, whose sheet is painted into the night (reference/act3-estate-sale/handback.md). The moon's colour as a multiply, then the hen a little darker and greyer, so she reads as a brown hen at night rather than in daylight, and the raccoon in the sitting sheet's cool grey.
